title.narrative: Output 2.3. Increased capacity of Member States to engage in a forward-looking international labour standards policy

description.narrative:
In In 2022, all reports due under ratified Conventions were received by the deadline of 1st September (C11, C29, C90, C100, C105, C138, C151, C182, MLC, 2006). Moreover, also in 2023, all reports under ratified Conventions were received by the deadline of 1st September (C88, C94, C96, C100, C111, C117). There is improvement in relation to previous years, as not all reports were received in 2021 (reports on the application on C11, C100 and C151 were not received in 2021). Moreover, some reports that were received in 2021, were not containing replies to the specific requests made by the CEACR. The perspectives for the sustainability of reporting are positive. In June 2022, the ILO facilitated the recruitment of an international consultant with funding from the Finnish Government (T4DW project) that supported the Government in collecting the relevant information to be included in all reports. In both 2022 and 2023 (between May and August of those years), draft reports sent by the Government were reviewed and some feedback provided on their content by the international consultant and the International Labour Standards Specialist to improve understanding of the requests made and the information that is expected for inclusion.
- Moreover, tripartite workshops were organized in August 2022 and August 2023, during which technical presentations were made by the International Labour Standards Specialist and the international consultant. These presentations concerned the Conventions for which a report was due (concerning among other themes, the forced labour and child labour and non-discrimination and equality Conventions), as well as the outstanding requests made by the CEACR in the reports requested. Discussions were held with the different Government officials, the representatives of the social partners and the participating ILO officials on the draft reports as prepared by the Government with the help of the consultant, which included discussions on numerous issues concerning implementation of the different Conventions.

Output 2.3. Increased capacity of Member States to engage in a forward-looking international labour standards policy

description.narrative: The Government initiated tripartite mechanisms enabling constituents to effectively engage in the implementation of ILS at the national level, including reporting to the supervisory bodies through the establishment of a tripartite multi-ministerial task team on reporting. In fact, the two workshops on reporting in August 2022 and August 2023, organized with ILO technical assistance, were instrumental in discussing a number of ILS-related issues, including legislative reform (ILO technical assistance is ongoing for the review of the Labour Act), ratifications (the Government, together with the social partners, is looking into the ratification of a number of Conventions, including C189 and C181), submissions and reporting on article 19 reports (in addition to the discussions, in a tripartite manner, on the article 22 reports). What is more, the Tripartite National Steering Committee on Child Labour validated a list of hazardous types of work prohibited to children under 18 and permissible light work for children entitles the Ghana Hazardous Activity Framework, which is now at the drafting stage, and for which an inclusion of a reference in the Labour Code, currently under review, is being worked upon ILO technical assistance was provided under funding from the Finnish Government for the Tripartite Reporting Training Workshop in August 2022 and August 2023 as well as for the meetings of the Tripartite National Steering Committee on Child Labour between August 2022 and August 2023. This support not only resulted in the timely reporting by 1st September in 2022 and 2023, but also significantly improved the quality of the reports, and built the capacity of the tripartite constituents on reporting, as well as the understanding of the principles in the relevant Conventions for the future.
